title: Vocabulary term
description: One canonical term of a governed vocabulary (`high-throughput` of `network_tier`, `gold` of `storage_tier`), keyed to (`vocabulary_kind`, `scope`). `scope` is a Class position, the portability contract (ADR-038 §3). `curation_state` puts it on the vocabulary-intake ladder (ADR-039). A FLOOR, NOT A LABEL (ADR-036): `requirements` carries the promise; matching is against it, never the string. NOT A TAXONOMY TERM: `Knowledge.TaxonomyTerm` carries a CATEGORY (what a thing IS), this a FLOOR (what it must MEET). `network_zone` is a taxonomy, `network_tier` a vocabulary term.

uuid.description: Frozen identity (ADR-051). A content change bumps `version`; the uuid never moves.

handle.description: The authoring name. A reference is AUTHORED by handle and RESOLVED to the uuid form (WIR-004) — never resolved by name alone.

version.description: A published (identity, version) is immutable: change the floor, bump the version. A consumer pinned to a version is pinned to the promise that version made.

vocabulary_kind.description: The vocabulary this term belongs to — `network_tier`, `storage_tier`, `os_image`, `vm_size`. Half the key. A `SharedDataElement` names this kind in `values.reference_data_type` to declare that its values are governed rather than an inline enum (ADR-038 §2).

scope.description: The Class scope this term is canonical AT: the other half of the key, and the portability contract (ADR-038 §3, ADR-058 §2). A term at `Network` holds for every Network provider; the same name at `NetworkFabric.AcmeSDN` holds only there. Portable reliance on a term requires it be canonical at a scope at least as general as the consumer's. That is checkable in a diff, not asserted in prose, and promoted by the governed contribution operation, not by editing a copy.

term.description: The selectable name — what a consumer writes. Portable because of what `requirements` says it means, not because the string matches.

curation_state.description: Where this term sits on the intake ladder. Whether an estate may BIND a term that is not yet `canonical` is a profile floor (ADR-007), not a property of the term.

requirements.description: The FLOOR the term denotes: what a provider must clear to qualify (ADR-036). Kind-specific by nature: a `network_tier` states bandwidth and latency minima, a `storage_tier` IOPS and throughput. Open by construction, because UDLM does not know every vocabulary an estate will govern; what it does know is that a term with no floor cannot be compared across estates, which is why at least one property is required. It is never a contribution to an assembled payload; nothing merges it.

status.description: Lifecycle, distinct from `curation_state`. A term can be `canonical` and `deprecated` at once: canonical says the ladder promoted it, deprecated says stop using it. Collapsing the two would make "retire a term" indistinguishable from "the ladder rejected it".

contributor.description: Who may author this term and the review it requires (federated-contribution-model §3).

supersedes.description: The term record(s) this one replaces, by uuid — never edit a published term, supersede it (ADR-051).

examples.name: Network tier — high throughput
examples.description: Governed definition of the 'high-throughput' network tier.

requirements.description: 10G-class or better with sub-millisecond intra-segment latency.
